# GitHub Pull Request #56

## Title
feat: prompt templates, tool exclusion, and overrides from extensions

## Description
Closes #52.

## Changes

- **Overrides** (`03f2533`): if an extension has a tool with the same name as an earlier tool, the later tool replaces it, as with pi's `registerTool`. The log now says `pi-durable extension X replaces tool bash from coding-tools`. The new `src/thread.test.ts` tests wraps of tools and sections and the order they apply in (the last wrap wins). It also tests hiding a tool with `callers: ["tools"]` and replacing a tool.
- **`exclude_tools` / `model_tools_hidden`** (`0cab9b8`): `exclude_tools` turns a tool off completely (`tools.remove`). `model_tools_hidden` keeps a tool away from the model, but other tools can still call it (`modelTools.remove`). Both accept `*` globs. Names are resolved after the extensions and their wraps are installed. A name that matches nothing gives a warning. If no tools are left for the model, the run fails. The inputs are applied on every run, so an empty input clears a setting from an earlier run. The `🤖` line now lists the tools the model gets.
- **Prompt templates** (`94b273d`): a task that starts with `/<name>` is replaced by that template, with `$1`…, `$ARGUMENTS`/`$@`, `${@:N[:L]}` and `${ARGUMENTS:-default}` filled in one pass. Templates come from three places, in this order:
  1. Each package's `pi.prompts`, including `pi.durable` packages.
  2. `.pi/prompts`, only with `trust_project`.
  3. `<agent_dir>/prompts`.

  If two templates have the same name, the first one wins and the others get a warning. Expansion applies to the first message (also `{{task}}`), to follow-ups, and to `prompt` for `pr_number` and direct runs. Answers to questions are not expanded. The log shows what was typed: `▶ Request from @alice: /pit-reflect focus (prompt template from pit)`. The comment entry stores it in its `typed` and `template` fields.
- **Docs**: `docs/extensions.md` (overrides, "Tools the model sees"), `docs/prompts.md` (prompt templates), `docs/security.md` (templates from the repository), `docs/how-it-works.md`, and the README input table.

## Not in this PR

- `model_tools_shown`: the docs say that the inputs only remove tools, so they can't bring back a tool that a wrap hid.
- The optional section that lists the templates for the model (the issue says it should be off by default).
- The pit change that hides the coding tools in `pit/durable` with wraps belongs in pit.

`npm run check` passes.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

+## Tools the model sees
+
+By default, the model gets all tools: the coding tools of pi-action (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`), then the tools of each pi-durable extension. Two inputs change this:

+| Input | Effect |
+|-------|--------|

+  with:

+    extensions: |

+    model_tools_hidden: read, write, edit, bash

+- pi-action applies the inputs on each run. When an input is empty, pi-action clears the setting of an earlier run on the thread.
+- The `🤖` line of the log shows the tools that the model gets, for example `🤖 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · tools: typescript · extensions: pit (typescript)`.

(pit asks with its `ui.*` globals, and also when it promotes a function to the project.) pi-action posts the question as a comment on the issue or pull request, and **the run ends**. An answer starts a new run, which continues the thread.

+A task that starts with `/<name>` can be a [prompt template](#prompt-templates).

+## Prompt templates
+
+When the task starts with `/<name>`, and a prompt template has that name, pi-action replaces the task with the template. This works as in pi's CLI. For example, `@pi /pit-reflect focus` gives pi the text of `pit-reflect.md`, with `focus` as its argument.
+
+pi-action loads templates from these places, in this sequence:
+
+1. The `pi.prompts` files and directories of each package in `extensions`, in the order of the input. This includes packages with a pi-durable extension.
+2. `.pi/prompts/*.md` in the repository, **only with `trust_project: true`**. See [Security](security.md#prompt-templates-from-the-repository).
+3. `<agent_dir>/prompts/*.md`, when `agent_dir` is set.
+
+The name of a template is its file name without `.md`. When two templates have the same name, the first one wins, and pi-action writes a warning. The log of the setup lists the templates.
+
+pi-action removes the frontmatter of the template (`description`, `argument-hint`), and replaces these variables with the arguments after `/<name>`:
+
+| Variable | Value |
+|----------|-------|
+| `$1` … `$9` | One argument. Empty when there is no such argument |
+| `$ARGUMENTS`, `$@` | All arguments, separated by spaces |
+| `${@:N}` | The arguments from argument N |
+| `${@:N:L}` | L arguments from argument N |
+| `${ARGUMENTS:-default}` | All arguments, or `default` when there are none |
+
+- Spaces separate the arguments. Quotes (`"..."`, `'...'`) keep spaces in one argument.
+- pi-action replaces all variables in one pass. A `$1` in an argument stays as it is.
+- pi-action expands templates in the [task](#the-task) of the first message (also `{{task}}` in `prompt_template`), of each follow-up, and in `prompt` (for `pr_number` runs and direct prompts). It does not expand answers to questions.
+- A `/<name>` that no template has stays as it is.
+- The log shows the request as it was typed, for example `▶ Request from @alice: /pit-reflect focus (prompt template from pit)`. The thread keeps the typed text in the `typed` field of the comment entry, and the name in `template`.

+// Prompt templates, as in pi: a request whose task starts with `/<name>` gets the template's body, with its arguments.
+import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
+import { basename, join } from "node:path";
+
+import type { Trigger } from "./triggers.ts";
+import type { Log } from "./types.ts";
+
+/** Where templates come from: Markdown files, or directories of them (one level deep). */
+export interface PromptSource {
+	/** Shown in the log: a package name, `.pi/prompts`, or `agent_dir`. */
+	source: string;
+	paths: readonly string[];
+}
+
+export interface PromptTemplate {
+	name: string;
+	source: string;
+	/** The file without its frontmatter. */
+	body: string;
+}
+
+/** The templates by name: the first source with a name wins. */
+export type PromptTemplates = ReadonlyMap<string, PromptTemplate>;
+
+const MARKDOWN = ".md";
+const FRONTMATTER = /^---\r?\n[\s\S]*?\r?\n---[ \t]*(?:\r?\n|$)/u;
+const WHITESPACE = /\s/u;
+const COMMAND = /^\/(?<name>[^\s/]+)(?:\s+(?<rest>[\s\S]*))?$/u;
+const PLACEHOLDER =
+	/\$\{@:(\d+)(?::(\d+))?\}|\$\{(?:ARGUMENTS|@):-([^}]*)\}|\$(ARGUMENTS|@|\d+)/gu;
+
+/** The Markdown files at `path`: the file itself, or the ones in the directory. */
+function markdownFiles(path: string): string[] {
+	if (!existsSync(path)) {
+		return [];
+	}
+	if (!statSync(path).isDirectory()) {
+		return path.endsWith(MARKDOWN) ? [path] : [];
+	}
+	return readdirSync(path, { withFileTypes: true })
+		.filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith(MARKDOWN))
+		.map((entry) => join(path, entry.name))
+		.toSorted();
+}
+
+/** A template file's text without its YAML frontmatter (`description`, `argument-hint`, ...). */
+export function stripFrontmatter(text: string): string {
+	return text.replace(FRONTMATTER, "").trim();
+}
+
+/**
+ * Loads the templates of every source, in order. The name is the file name without `.md`. When names collide, the
+ * first one wins and the log says which ones it hides.
+ */
+export function loadPromptTemplates(
+	sources: readonly PromptSource[],
+	log: Log,
+): Map<string, PromptTemplate> {
+	const templates = new Map<string, PromptTemplate>();
+	for (const { source, paths } of sources) {
+		for (const file of paths.flatMap((path) => markdownFiles(path))) {
+			const name = basename(file, MARKDOWN);
+			const taken = templates.get(name);
+			if (taken === undefined) {
+				const body = stripFrontmatter(readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
+				templates.set(name, { name, source, body });
+			} else {
+				log.warning(
+					`Prompt template /${name} from ${source} is ignored: ${taken.source} has one with that name`,
+				);
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return templates;
+}
+
+/** The arguments of a template command, split as a shell would: on whitespace, with '...' and "..." kept whole. */
+export function parseArguments(text: string): string[] {
+	const args: string[] = [];
+	let current = "";
+	let quote: string | undefined;
+	let started = false;
+	for (const char of text) {
+		if (quote !== undefined) {
+			if (char === quote) {
+				quote = undefined;
+			} else {
+				current += char;
+			}
+		} else if (char === '"' || char === "'") {
+			quote = char;
+			started = true;
+		} else if (WHITESPACE.test(char)) {
+			if (started) {
+				args.push(current);
+			}
+			current = "";
+			started = false;
+		} else {
+			current += char;
+			started = true;
+		}
+	}
+	if (started) {
+		args.push(current);
+	}
+	return args;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Puts the arguments into a template's body, in one pass (an argument that contains `$1` stays as it is): `$1`...
+ * for one argument, `$ARGUMENTS` and `$@` for all, `${@:N}` for all from the Nth (`${@:N:L}`: L of them), and
+ * `${ARGUMENTS:-default}` for all, or the default when there are none.
+ */
+export function substituteArguments(
+	body: string,
+	args: readonly string[],
+): string {
+	const all = args.join(" ");
+	const expand = (
+		_match: string,
+		start: string | undefined,
+		length: string | undefined,
+		fallback: string | undefined,
+		name: string | undefined,
+	): string => {
+		if (start !== undefined) {
+			const from = Math.max(Number(start) - 1, 0);
+			const to = length === undefined ? undefined : from + Number(length);
+			return args.slice(from, to).join(" ");
+		}
+		if (fallback !== undefined) {
+			return args.length > 0 ? all : fallback;
+		}
+		if (name === "ARGUMENTS" || name === "@") {
+			return all;
+		}
+		return args[Number(name) - 1] ?? "";
+	};
+	return body.replaceAll(PLACEHOLDER, expand);
+}
+
+/**
+ * The trigger with its task expanded, when the task starts with `/<name>` of a template; the trigger as it is
+ * otherwise (an unknown `/name` stays text). Answers to questions are never templates.
+ */
+export function expandTrigger(
+	trigger: Trigger,
+	templates: PromptTemplates,
+): Trigger {
+	const match = trigger.answer ? undefined : COMMAND.exec(trigger.task.trim());
+	const template = templates.get(match?.groups?.["name"] ?? "");
+	if (template === undefined) {
+		return trigger;
+	}
+	const args = parseArguments(match?.groups?.["rest"] ?? "");
+	return {
+		...trigger,
+		task: substituteArguments(template.body, args),
+		template: {
+			name: template.name,
+			source: template.source,
+			typed: trigger.task,
+		},
+	};
+}

+// The `exclude_tools` and `model_tools_hidden` inputs: which tools a thread's model is offered, and which exist at all.
+import type { Log } from "./types.ts";
+
+/** Tool name patterns from the inputs; `*` matches any run of characters. */
+export interface ToolSelection {
+	/** `exclude_tools`: these tools are disabled; neither the model nor other tools can call them. */
+	exclude: readonly string[];
+	/** `model_tools_hidden`: the model is not offered these tools; other tools (pit's `tools.*`) can still call them. */
+	hidden: readonly string[];
+}
+
+/** What a selection resolves to against the thread's tools. */
+export interface ToolPlan {
+	/** The tools to disable. */
+	exclude: string[];
+	/** The tools to hide from the model. */
+	hide: string[];
+	/** The tools the model is offered, in order. */
+	offered: string[];
+}
+
+const SPECIAL = /[.+?^${}()|[\]\\]/gu;
+
+/** A matcher for one `*` glob: the whole name must match. */
+function compilePattern(pattern: string): RegExp {
+	const source = pattern
+		.replaceAll(SPECIAL, String.raw`\$&`)
+		.replaceAll("*", ".*");
+	return new RegExp(`^${source}$`, "u");
+}
+
+/** The names among `names` that `patterns` match, in order; writes a warning for each pattern that matches none. */
+function matching(
+	input: string,
+	patterns: readonly string[],
+	names: readonly string[],
+	log: Log,
+): string[] {
+	const matched = new Set<string>();
+	for (const pattern of patterns) {
+		const regex = compilePattern(pattern);
+		const hits = names.filter((name) => regex.test(name));
+		if (hits.length === 0) {
+			log.warning(`${input}: "${pattern}" matches no tool`);
+		}
+		for (const hit of hits) {
+			matched.add(hit);
+		}
+	}
+	return names.filter((name) => matched.has(name));
+}
+
+/**
+ * Resolve the selection against the thread's tools: `all` (every enabled tool, after the wraps) and `offered` (the ones
+ * the model gets without a selection). Throws if the selection leaves the model with no tools.
+ */
+export function planTools(
+	selection: ToolSelection,
+	all: readonly string[],
+	offered: readonly string[],
+	log: Log,
+): ToolPlan {
+	const exclude = matching("exclude_tools", selection.exclude, all, log);
+	const hide = matching("model_tools_hidden", selection.hidden, all, log);
+	const removed = new Set([...exclude, ...hide]);
+	const kept = offered.filter((name) => !removed.has(name));
+	if (kept.length === 0 && removed.size > 0) {
+		throw new Error(
+			`exclude_tools and model_tools_hidden leave the model with no tools (it would have ${offered.join(", ")})`,
+		);
+	}
+	return { exclude, hide, offered: kept };
+}
